prize_parts.citation: for the development of halide perovskites as solution-processable semiconductors for high-efficiency solar cells

statement.case_for: Halide perovskites are a new class of semiconductor absorber with a clear physical principle behind them: strong absorption, long carrier diffusion lengths, defect tolerance and a tunable band gap. Efficiency rose from a few percent to over 25% in roughly a decade, and the same material platform now supports tandem cells, LEDs and detectors. That is the kind of generative capability I weigh heavily, and it can be explained to a broad audience in a single sentence. The attribution has a defensible chronology: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell in 2009, Park the first stable solid-state cell in 2012, and Snaith showed the thin-film architecture that revealed the intrinsic transport properties. The science of efficiency has been reproduced by thousands of groups.
statement.case_against: Credit is genuinely contested. Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis all have strong claims, and any three-person cut will look arbitrary to part of the community. Operational stability and lead content remain unresolved, so the commercial maturity is still partial. Only three of eight members ranked it, so the committee has not endorsed it as broadly as it has the lipid nanoparticle candidate, which all four of its supporters placed second. There is also a fair objection that this is materials physics rather than core chemistry. I come from the physics side, so I may be too generous about that.

responses.point: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (B021) is a general, ligand-controlled method used routinely in medicinal and process chemistry, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide chemistry is a precursor requiring stoichiometric tin rather than an equal claim.
responses.response: I take the impact argument seriously and the Buchwald and Hartwig pairing is cleaner than anything I can offer for perovskites. My qualification is the 2010 prize: the committee would have to explain why C-N coupling is a distinct discovery and not a later extension of Pd cross-coupling. I also want to see whether Kosugi's 1983 work is a priority issue or only a precursor, because that decides whether the citation can name only two people. If you can show the ligand-design step is the discovery, I would move B021 into my top tier. I do not yet see that it beats the perovskite case on generative potential.

responses.point: Base editing (B052) is a new chemical approach to genome editing that has already reached clinical trials, with Liu as the intellectual driver and Komor and Gaudelli doing the decisive first experiments as trainees.
responses.response: I ranked B052 third and still think the deaminase-Cas chemistry is real and elegant. I disagree that it is ready now. Coming just after the 2020 CRISPR prize it will look like a refinement to many readers, and clinical efficacy data are still preliminary. The Kondo and Nishida work also complicates the credit. Your three-name proposal gives the base editors more credit than it gives the independent deaminase-Cas work. Please say why Komor and Gaudelli should be credited ahead of Kondo and Nishida when the question is who made the discovery. Your support for perovskites with Miyasaka, Park and Snaith is welcome, and I note we agree on that trio.

responses.point: Massively parallel sequencing (B028) turned DNA reading into a routine chemical measurement through reversible terminators and clonal clusters, and Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Rothberg are the core originators.
responses.response: This is probably the candidate with the most thoroughly validated impact, and I accept that the enabling steps are chemical. My concern is attribution. Solexa chemistry, 454 pyrosequencing, colony sequencing and Ju's terminators are parallel inventions, and your list adds Rothberg to Balasubramanian and Klenerman, which still leaves Ju and Mayer out. A citation that stays accurate has to say which step the committee honours. If we frame it as sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators, I could support Balasubramanian and Klenerman. If it is the platform that scaled sequencing, the claim becomes broader and murkier. I would also point out that nanopore sequencing, my fourth choice, is a physically distinct route to the same goal and the committee should not mix them.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B058) rest on lipid self-assembly and phase behavior, with Cullis, Hope and Madden building the encapsulation and ionizable-lipid methods and a real impact on siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines.
responses.response: I put B058 second, so I largely agree with you on its science and impact. The difficulty is that your trio of Cullis, Hope and Madden differs from the trio that Aili and I proposed, which adds Anderson and Langer and leaves out Hope and Madden. That shows how unsettled the attribution is. I also think the 2023 Medicine prize makes the framing important: the citation must be about lipid design and delivery, not mRNA itself. I would like you to say whether the founding formulation work of Hope and Madden outweighs the later combinatorial libraries of Anderson and Langer. If we can settle that, B058 is the candidate most likely to command a majority.

uncertainties: Whether a three-person perovskite prize can be defended against Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis.
Whether the committee would treat B058 as lipid chemistry distinct from the 2023 Medicine prize, and who the three credited names should be.
Whether C-N coupling (B021) is distinct enough from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize, and how Kosugi's work should be treated.
Whether the base-editing field (B052) is mature enough soon after the 2020 CRISPR prize, and how to allocate credit between the Liu group and Kondo and Nishida.
I am relying on my own recollection of timelines and have not independently verified them.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I work in Lund on nanowire and thermoelectric physics, and none of the shortlisted candidates is a collaborator or from my institution as far as the profile shows. Fellow Lund committee members Somfai and Sparr share my institution but this is not a recusal issue for any candidate.
